result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.

result.rule: When the description states that an action performed by one participant sends a message to another participant, or that another participant's start or wait point depends on that action, whether the other participant is a peer in the process or an external party acting on its own: Model each participant as its own pool in one collaboration. Draw every cross-participant dependency as a message flow from the sending participant's task (or throw event) to a message start event or intermediate message catch event in the receiving participant's pool. Do not connect elements of different pools with sequence flows. Do not connect a sending task to a catch event inside the same pool with a message flow. Do not reverse the flow so that the receiving start or catch event is the source.

When the description states that a later step can only begin after replies or a list are received from other people (for example 'as soon as you have received a list', or 'until all people reply'), so the wait for that arrival comes between the request and the next step: Model the wait for the other people's replies as an intermediate catch event placed after the activity that gathers the information and before the step that depends on it. Connect the event's incoming flow from the gathering activity and its outgoing flow to the dependent step. Do not omit the wait, and do not replace it with a task.

When the description says the process offers a set of options or a request to an external party, such as a customer, and that party then returns its choices before the process can continue: Model the offer as a sendTask, and model the returned choices as a receiveTask placed immediately after it in the main sequence and before any task that works on those choices. Do not model the returned choices as a new start event, because the process has already begun, and do not let the send step stand in for the return.

When the description says that the recipient of a delivered item has to confirm receipt before the process can continue: After the activity that delivers the item, model the awaited confirmation from the recipient as an intermediate message catch event that gates the subsequent flow, placed in the sequence after the delivery activity. Do not model the wait as a task, and do not omit it.

result.process_description:
Title: Building a House

You want to build a tree house.
First you collect your requirements, and send them to a tree house architect.
The architect sends you back a draft, which you refine multiple times with additional requirements.
You then create the list of needed materials from the plan.
These materials fall into several categories, you order them from several online stores.
While the order is processed, you send messages to several of your friends to build the house.
After the house is built, you send invitations for a tree house party to your friends.
In order to buy the snacks for the party, a list of people that attend the party is created.

When the description says an external party (such as a customer) has provided information, and the producer then performs a distinct step that works on that information (for example determining, specifying or preparing items from it): Model the arrival of the information as an event (a message start event or an intermediate catch event, as the description implies), and keep the producer's subsequent step as its own activity placed after that event. Use a userTask or manualTask according to whether the description states software support. Do not let the receipt event replace the step that works on the information.

When the description says that information must be obtained from several external parties (for example their quantities, prices and delivery times) before a decision can be made: Model the request to the external parties as a send step, and add a separate step that receives or collects their answers before the decision gateway that depends on them. A wait for an answer is an intermediate catch event or a receive task, and the consolidation of the answers is an activity of its own. Do not connect the send step directly to the decision gateway.

When the description is written from the first-person view of a performing role that sends a request to an external party, and that party then acts on its own by paying, objecting, or letting a deadline pass, so the performing role must react to what the party does: Model the performing role as its own bpmn:participant pool and the external party as a separate bpmn:participant pool in the same collaboration. Connect the request sent by the performing role to the external party with a message flow, and connect the payment or objection returned by the external party back to the performing role with a message flow. Keep the performing role's internal steps, such as checking the case and closing it, inside its own pool.
